lsp — MCP server (poly-lsp-mcp mcp --root /work)

Tools:

Use help("lsp.toolName") for full details on any tool.

help_ns.text:
Html — CSS selector querying and HTML parsing (namespaced as Html.*) TYPICAL: Query elements Html.select("

hello

", "p") // → [{text, html, tag, attrs}] Web.fetch(url).body |> Html.select("h1") |> map(h => h.text) TYPICAL: Links / text / tables Html.links(page) // → [{text, href}] Html.text("

Hi there

") Html.table(page, "table.data") // → [{col: val, ...}] using as keys CSS SELECTORS: tag, .class, #id, [attr], tag > child, tag child, selector1, selector2

help.text:
abs(n: number) — absolute value
  addNode(parent: node|string, type: string, props?: object) — adds a node connected from parent. Edge type defaults to node type
  assert(message: string, condition: any) — fails if condition is falsy
  at(input: array|string, index: number) — element at index (supports negative)
  avg(input: array) — arithmetic mean of an array of numbers
  bool(value: any) — → boolean
  both(input: node|array, type?: string) — follows edges in both directions
  ceil(n: number) — rounds up
  charAt(input: string, index: number) — character at index
  chunk(input: array, size: number) — splits into sub-arrays of size n
  concat(a: array, b: array) — concatenates two arrays
  contains(input: array|string, value: any) — membership test
  countBy(input: array, fn?: (T) => string) — → {key: count}; fn defaults to identity
  difference(a: array, b: array) — elements in a not in b
  endsWith(input: string, suffix: string) — suffix test
  entries(input: object) — object → [[key, value], ...] (JS-compatible)
  every(input: array, fn: (T) => boolean) — true if all elements match
  extendLimit(opts: {steps?: number, timeout?: number, callDepth?: number, outputBytes?: number}) — increases execution limits for this eval. Call before heavy computation
  fail(msg?: string) — throws error
  fill(input: array, value: any, start?: number, end?: number) — fills array with value, returns new array
  filter(input: array|object, fn: (T, index?) => boolean) — keeps elements where fn is truthy; on objects filters entries with (value, key)
  find(input: array, fn: (T) => boolean) — first match or null
  flat(input: array) — flattens one level
  flatMap(input: array, fn: (T) => array) — maps then flattens one level
  floor(n: number) — rounds down
  forEach(input: array, fn: (T, index?) => void) — applies fn to each element, returns null
  fromEntries(input: array) — [[key, value]] or [{key, value}] → object
  groupBy(input: array, fn: (T) => string) — → {key: elements[]}
  help(search?: string) — list commands; search by name
  inE(input: node|array, type?: string) — gets incoming edges as objects
  inbound(input: node|array, type?: string) — follows incoming edges, returns source nodes
  indexOf(input: array|string, value: any) — first index of value, or -1
  intersection(a: array, b: array) — elements in both a and b
  isArray(value: any) — true if value is an array
  join(input: array, sep?: string) — joins elements with separator
  keys(input: object) — object keys
  last(input: array|string, n?: number) — last n elements (default 1 element, not wrapped)
  lastIndexOf(input: string, substr: string) — last index of substring, or -1
  len(input: array|string|object) — length
  limit(input: array|string, n: number) — first n elements
  limits() — shows current execution limits
  lines(input: string) — splits string into lines (trims trailing empty line)
  link(from: node|string, to: node|string, type?: string, props?: object) — creates an edge between two nodes
  lower(input: string) — → lowercase
  map(input: array|object, fn: (T, index?) => U) — applies fn to each element (with optional index); on objects maps values with (value, key)
  match(input: string, pattern: string|regex) — JS-compatible regex match: non-global → [fullMatch, group1, ...] or null; global → [match1, ...]
  max(...values: number[]) — maximum
  min(...values: number[]) — minimum
  node(id: string) — gets a node by id
  nodes(type?: string) — gets all nodes, optionally filtered by type
  num(value: any) — → number
  out(input: node|array, type?: string) — follows outgoing edges, returns target nodes
  outE(input: node|array, type?: string) — gets outgoing edges as objects
  padEnd(input: string, length: number, fill?: string) — pads end to target length
  padStart(input: string, length: number, fill?: string) — pads start to target length
  parseJson(input: string) — JSON string → value (loose: bare keys + trailing commas OK; values stay strict — no bare words)
  pow(base: number, exp: number) — exponentiation
  print(...values: any) — prints, returns last
  product(input: array) — product of an array of numbers (empty → 1)
  profile(fn: () => any) — runs fn with cost tracing; returns {result, steps, lines: [{line, steps}]} sorted by cost
  range(end: number | start: number, end: number) — [start, end) integer array (single arg: range(0, end))
  reduce(input: array, fn: (acc, T, index?) => acc, init?: any = 0) — folds array to single value
  removeNode(node: node|string) — removes a node and all its edges
  replace(input: string, old: string|regex, new: string) — replaces occurrences (string literal or regex with $1 backrefs)
  reverse(input: array|string) — reverses
  root() — returns the graph root node
  round(n: number) — rounds
  setProps(target: node|edge|string, props: object) — merges properties into a node or edge
  shuffle(input: array) — randomly reorders array elements
  skip(input: array|string, n: number) — drops first n elements
  slice(input: array|string, start: number, end?: number) — extracts section
  some(input: array, fn: (T) => boolean) — true if any element matches
  sort(input: array, keyOrComparator?: string | (a, b) => number) — sorts; string key for objects, comparator fn, or "desc"/"asc" for direction
  split(input: string, sep?: string|regex) — splits by separator; default: ,
  startsWith(input: string, prefix: string) — prefix test
  str(value: any) — → string
  substring(input: string, start: number, end?: number) — slice string
  sum(input: array) — sums an array of numbers (empty → 0)
  test(input: string, pattern: string|regex) — boolean regex test
  toArray(value: any, mapFn?: (v, i) => T) — array-like→array; supports {length: n} and optional mapFn
  toJson(input: any) — value → JSON string
  trim(input: string) — strips whitespace
  typeof(value: any) — type name
  union(a: array, b: array) — combined, deduplicated
  unique(input: array) — deduplicates
  unlink(edge: edge|string) — removes an edge by id
  upper(input: string) — → uppercase
  values(input: object) — object values
  xor(a: number, b: number) — bitwise XOR
  zip(a: array, b: array) — pairs elements from two arrays

  Html:
    Html.links(html: string, selector?: string) — extracts links. Returns [{text, href}]. Optional selector filters
    Html.select(html: string, selector: string) — queries HTML with CSS selector. Returns [{text, html, tag, attrs}]
    Html.table(html: string, selector?: string) — extracts HTML table as array of objects. Uses <th> for keys, falls back to col0, col1
    Html.text(html: string) — extracts visible text from HTML, stripping all tags

  Web:
    Web.clearCache() — clears the HTTP response cache. Returns number of entries cleared
    Web.fetch(url: string, opts?: {method?: string, headers?: object, body?: string, parse?: string, noCache?: boolean}) — HTTP request. Returns {status, headers, body}. parse: "json" auto-parses body. GET responses cached 60s
    Web.fetchText(url: string) — fetches URL and extracts visible text (strips HTML)
    Web.search(query: string, opts?: {limit?: number}) — web search via DuckDuckGo. Returns [{title, url, snippet}]

  lsp:
    lsp.node_edit(node: string, oldText?: string, newText?: string, rename?: string, params?: array, return?: string, delete?: boolean, accept?: string, includeComments?: boolean, resolution?: object) — Edit one node of the projection. node = an address from node_query's matches[].node, or a selector matching exactly one node (2+ errors and lists candidates).
RENAMING a symbol? Use the rename op — ONE call renames the declaration AND every usage across the WHOLE workspace, atomically. Do NOT rename by hand-editing files one at a time with oldText/newText: that misses usages and leaves the build broken between edits.
Exactly ONE op:
rename:"NewName" — workspace-wide semantic rename; lexical guesses reported under candidates, never applied.
oldText+newText — replace a snippet inside the node. oldText must occur exactly once in the node; the address scopes it, so it need only be unique WITHIN that node — keep it short. Pass the node's whole text to rewrite it entirely, or that text + a new declaration to ADD one next to it.
newText alone — REPLACES a span address (@start-end: ::body/::signature/::grep/a conflict); CREATES a file at a new path; refused on a symbol (use oldText) and never inserts one.
delete:true — excise the node.
accept:"mine"|"theirs" — resolve merge conflicts (whole file, or one block by its @start-end span); markers go too. A conflicted file indexes both sides as PEERS; ::conflict/::mine/::theirs/::base read them apart (sides carry their ref).
params [{name,type}] / return — rebuild the parameter list / return type (go/typescript/python).
includeComments / resolution:{mode,target} — rename only.
    lsp.node_query(selector: string, limit?: integer, offset?: integer, budget?: any) — CSS-inspired selector language over ONE tree — DAG: project > dir > file > symbols (dotted) > argument — plus the reference GRAPH as pseudo-elements. Files are nodes; no separate filesystem API.
TAGS are a FIXED set: project dir file func method type struct interface class const var field enum ctor module import argument, *. Workspace NAMES are NEVER tags, always #ids: #cache, #'store.go#Save' (quote with '). Language as class: file.go. space=descendant >=child ,=union — space is ALWAYS a node boundary. FILTER by bracketing ONTO an element: func[path=a.go] ≠ func path=a.go (things inside a func). In [] | is OR and & AND over whole TESTS — but ONLY before another test: [name=a|name=b] is boolean, [name~=a|b] is one regex.
GRAPH: X::in who points at X / X::out what X's body points at; kind class .call/.type/.import. The far end is the edge's CHILD — cross with >. X::out = X's own edges, X ::out = nested symbols' too. {m,n} on an edge = edges crossed, {1,} = transitive.
::grep('flags pattern') = matched LINES as nodes (-i -w -E -F -v -A/-B/-C<n>; literal unless -E); no ctx by default (hit=the line), -A/-B/-C adds it; result carries a per-file rollup.
FOOTGUNS: * NEVER matches ::edges or ::grep lines — name them or they're invisible. {m,n} elsewhere is regex REPETITION child-joined, NOT depth: func{2} = func>func; within-3-levels = "> *{0,2} > x". :not/:is(sel) test the node ITSELF; :where/:any/:all/:empty(sel) test AROUND it (leading tag = a descendant, leading ::/pseudo = the node; bare :any/:all/:empty judge their position). :parents(sel) = ALL upstream (ancestors + incoming refs) — broader than callers. Edge/::grep addresses are file@line: node_read/node_edit hit that exact line.
RECIPES: START at a name/string: ::grep('needle'), method[name=x] — NOT :root > * (dir listing). #'a.go#Save'::in.call callers | #'main'::out.call > * callees | func:not([name^=Test]):empty(::in) dead code | import#huma::in.call::grep('-E (Get|Post)\(') endpoints.
selector "?" = the full grammar.
    lsp.node_read(node: string, startLine?: integer, lineLimit?: integer) — Read a node whole. node = an address from node_query's matches[].node ("<file>#<sym>" or "<file>"), or a selector matching exactly one node (2+ errors and lists candidates).
An addressed symbol is NEVER truncated: you get the complete declaration, byte-for-byte the span node_edit's newText replaces.
startLine/lineLimit on ANY address read a file WINDOW anchored there — not the text oldText matches; it says so.
